faqs.title: How long the withdrawals take?
faqs.description: bSyrupUSDC normally have instant liquidity, but in rare cases withdrawals can take around 24h with the maximum possible time being 30 days. You can see the available funds to withdraw in the Liquidity section above.

faqs.title: What is the bsyrupUSDC Vault?
faqs.description: The bsyrupUSDC vault gives you on-chain exposure to syrupUSDC, Maple Finance's permissionless yield product backed by fixed-rate, overcollateralised loans to institutional borrowers. You deposit USDC and receive bSyrupUSDC, a vault share token whose value reflects syrupUSDC held on your behalf as borrower interest accrues.

faqs.title: What is bsyrupUSDC and how is it different from syrupUSDC?
faqs.description: syrupUSDC is Maple's liquid yield-bearing token representing exposure to Maple's institutional lending pools. bSyrupUSDC is Byzanlink's vault share token: when you deposit USDC, the vault allocates into syrupUSDC via Maple's infrastructure and issues bsyrupUSDC to track your share of the strategy. Yield compounds through the underlying syrupUSDC position rather than a fixed $1 token price.

faqs.title: How is yield generated?
faqs.description: Yield comes from interest paid by institutional borrowers on Maple's digital asset lending platform. Loans are fixed-rate, overcollateralised, and typically short duration, which supports consistent income relative to many DeFi lending markets. Displayed APY reflects base yield and may change with market conditions; it is illustrative, not guaranteed.

faqs.title: How do I deposit into the vault?
faqs.description: Connect a supported wallet, select USDC as the input token, enter an amount, and confirm the deposit. The vault mints bsyrupUSDC representing your share. Under the hood, USDC is routed into Maple's syrupUSDC strategy through Maple's onchain infrastructure and dedicated pools segmented from Maple's existing institutional customer pools.

faqs.title: What is the redemption period?
faqs.description: The vault targets a 3-day redemption window under normal conditions. Underlying syrupUSDC liquidity is usually available quickly; in stressed conditions, settlement may take longer (Maple cites up to ~24 hours in rare cases and a maximum of 30 days in extreme scenarios). Available liquidity for withdrawals is shown in the Liquidity section on the vault page.

faqs.title: How are loans collateralised and monitored?
faqs.description: All underlying Maple loans are overcollateralised. Maple operates monitoring systems designed to keep collateralisation ratios healthy across market conditions. Lending still carries credit, liquidity, and smart contract risk; collateralisation reduces but does not eliminate the risk of loss.

faqs.title: What are the main risks?
faqs.description: This vault operates on Ethereum mainnet with real USDC. Risks include borrower default, market or liquidity stress affecting redemptions, smart contract vulnerabilities, and strategy or protocol changes. Only deposit funds you are willing to allocate to this strategy. Past yield is not a guarantee of future performance.

faqs.title: Is bsyrupUSDC the same as holding USDC?
faqs.description: No. bsyrupUSDC is a yield-bearing vault share tied to Maple's syrupUSDC lending exposure, not a 1:1 USDC claim at all times. You deposit USDC to enter the strategy; value is driven by the underlying loan pool and can move up or down. Neither Circle nor any third party guarantees vault or Maple loan performance.

faqs.title: What is Byzanlink's relationship with Maple and Circle?
faqs.description: Byzanlink integrates Maple Finance infrastructure to offer syrupUSDC exposure through this vault. There is no formal partnership or affiliation between Maple's syrupUSDC product and Circle Internet Financial or its related entities. "USDC" is a registered trademark of Circle; use here describes the stablecoin you may deposit. Maple develops the underlying protocol; Byzanlink provides the vault interface and bsyrupUSDC share token.
